summary: PCIe I/O noise from co-tenant workload caused autoscaler shrink oscillation in dedicated pool
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-08 09:42 UTC PineTrack reported elevated p99 latency and repeated autoscaler shrinks in their dedicated pool during a scheduled usage window. Impact: sustained p99 from ~220ms -> 1.2s for text-generation routes and intermittent 503 errors for higher-concurrency sessions. Users saw degraded throughput and dropped streams for ~40 minutes. Environment: Dedicated pool (prod-us-east), customer pinned to redwood/compat-13b, autoscaler policy: aggressive scale-down (idle_threshold=30s).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route steady multi-tenant load to dedicated pool with concurrent short streams (50-100 streams/s). 2) In same pool, schedule a background artifact-scanner (IO heavy) to perform frequent NVMe reads/writes. 3) Observe p99 and kernel latency on serving hosts, autoscaler perceives reduced effective throughput and initiates scale-down. 4) After scale-down, load remains high and p99 spikes further, autoscaler then ramps back up causing oscillation.
logs: Support logs: host/gpu metrics show PCIe transfer latency spikes correlated with artifact-scanner start (logs: /logs/pinetrack/2026-03-08/pci-latency-0942.log). Autoscaler events: scale-down at 09:45 UTC (decision: low-util), scale-up at 09:48 UTC, repeated twice. Kernel traces: increased DMA wait times and NVMe queue depth jumps. Monitoring graphs: https://grafana.redwood/s/teams/pool/dedicated-us-east?from=2026-03-08T09:30Z&to=2026-03-08T10:30Z
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: noisy tenant causing GPU compute stalls. Collected perf counters (PCIe DMA latency) and NVMe IO metrics; found tight correlation between background-scanner IO bursts and GPU DMA tail latency. Autoscaler logic evaluated endpoint throughput and decided to scale down because of apparent drop in processed requests; scale-down window too aggressive for transient IO noise. SRE replayed scaled-down decision on historical metrics and reproduced oscillation. Tenant isolation layer allowed heavy NVMe IO within same node, contributing to PCIe contention. Cross-checked with disk-IO QoS metrics: absent for dedicated pool nodes. No kernel panics or GPU driver crashes found. Related change identified: a recent infra rollout (PR infra/rg-autoscaler#4123) reduced scale-down hysteresis to improve cost; this made the pool susceptible to transient drops.
resolution: Mitigation applied (2026-03-08 10:02 UTC): 1) Temporarily pinned PineTrack traffic to a warm sub-pool with IO-QoS enforced. 2) SRE disabled aggressive scale-down (increase idle_threshold to 120s) for the affected dedicated cluster. 3) Requested customer to postpone artifact-scanner runs while we validated isolation fixes. Permanent fixes: 1) Rollout IO-QoS enforcement on dedicated pool nodes to limit NVMe burst impact (PR infra/rg-qos#119). 2) Update autoscaler to incorporate PCIe and IO anomaly signals into scale decisions (ticketed as INT-331220). 3) Add runbook entry for noisy-IO detection and automated temporary routing. Customer notified and confirmed service returned to baseline by 10:35 UTC. Follow-ups: monitor for 72 hours and coordinate downtime window to deploy QoS kernel parameters.
